description: This is update number 17 in the US Department of Energy's series of situation reports on Hurricane Ian, issued at 11:00 AM EDT on 6 October 2022 for public distribution, eight days after the Category 4 landfall near Fort Myers, Florida, and a second landfall near Georgetown, South Carolina. The electricity summary reports about 208,000 customer outages remaining in Florida, down 92 percent from the peak of 2.7 million on 29 September, more than 44,000 workers from 33 states and the District of Columbia at peak, damage mainly to distribution, not transmission, and areas needing rebuild where customer structures are damaged. The oil and natural gas summary says ports and fuel terminals reopened while some retail stations stayed unavailable, and a table lists federal and state emergency declarations and hours-of-service waivers by state. Access: free PDF on the energy.gov site; no licence is stated. Coverage is the US Southeast for one date. Caveats: it is a three-page snapshot narrative, not a data series, and figures changed in other updates. It suits resilience and emergency response studies of storm impacts on distribution networks and fuel supply, and it relates to the Hurricane Ida situation update catalogued here as data-doe-ceser-hurricane-ida-situation-update-10-2021.
